title: A Blueprint for Weird Teachers, Schools, and Districts
author: Science of Reading Classroom
source: Science of Reading Classroom Substack, January 26, 2026
summary: Effective teachers share intense curiosity that drives continuous tinkering with instruction and content, constant learning despite success, and seeking connections with like-minded peers. School leaders cultivate curiosity by allocating regular paid time for discussing instructional practice, maintaining focus on pedagogy, structuring conversations around shared texts, building explicit experimentation culture, and identifying high-performing teachers to give them agency to lead others.
points: The smartest teachers share intense curiosity despite systems not rewarding it; they constantly tinker and look to scale their work beyond their classroom.
School leaders must allocate regular, dedicated, paid contract time specifically for instructional practice discussion; without time, teachers cannot develop curiosity.
Professional development should focus on instructional practice using shared texts and require teachers to try routines in their contexts, then debrief application.
Leaders should explicitly encourage experimentation; high-performing teachers often use approaches bumping against rules, and finding these is the entry point for systemic change.
Leaders identify high performers via student data, give them agency and visibility, and position them to teach others; that is how culture of excellence begins.
